reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cadherins -> form adherens junctions -> join epithelial cells to each other -> 95% CHAIN: Integrins -> connect extracellular matrix to the cell cytoskeleton -> not directly involved in joining epithelial cells to each other -> 70% CHAIN: Fibronectins -> bind to integrins -> help in cell adhesion and migration -> not directly involved in joining epithelial cells to each other -> 60% CHAIN: Elastins -> provide elasticity to tissues -> not involved in joining epithelial cells to each other -> 50% CHAIN: Laminins -> major components of basement membranes -> provide structural support to epithelial cells -> indirectly contribute to the connection between epithelial cells -> 95%
enhanced_information: Cadherins are the molecules that join epithelial cells to each other by forming adherens junctions. Integrins, although important in connecting the extracellular matrix to the cell cytoskeleton, are not directly involved in joining epithelial cells to each other. Fibronectins bind to integrins and aid in cell adhesion and migration but are not directly involved in connecting epithelial cells. Elastins provide tissue elasticity and are not involved in joining epithelial cells. Laminins, as major components of basement membranes, indirectly contribute to the connection between epithelial cells by providing structural support.
analysis: Cadherins are the molecules specifically known for joining epithelial cells to each other by forming adherens junctions. Integrins play a role in connecting the extracellular matrix to the cell cytoskeleton, fibronectins bind to integrins aiding in cell adhesion and migration, elastins provide tissue elasticity, and laminins contribute to the connection indirectly by providing structural support. Therefore, the most likely correct option for joining epithelial cells to each other is Cadherins.
